chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Written arrangements adapted to the band's style
summary: Stanley says some written arrangements were stiffer than the heads; McShann says the players made them sound like the band's own way.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Some of the written arrangements would be less in your style than really the heads were.
Well, I think that some of the arrangements that Tadd and people wrote were perhaps rather more formal and therefore they'd come out stiffer than the heads.
Well, that's true. But it was one thing that I did like about the guys, like you say, they would be formal, stiff arrangements, but when those cats got through with them --
Yeah, well, they got them really down.
When they got through with the arrangements, it was back to what we was doing.
You know, probably wasn't written that way. It wasn't written that way.
But we made it that way.
They adapted it to your style.
